area-1.name: Procedures compliance
area-1.OSO1.hint:
Ensure that your organization has a documented and verifiable cybersecurity policy. This policy should support the development of secure software with digital elements, define clear procedures for identifying, addressing, and resolving vulnerabilities, and encourage the voluntary reporting of vulnerabilities by developers, as outlined in Article 15.

The policy should also consider the specific nature of your role as an open-source steward, including any legal or organizational structures you are subject to. Additionally, it should promote the sharing of information about discovered vulnerabilities within the open-source community.
area-1.OSO1.questions.Q1.text: Do open-source stewards document and verify a cybersecurity policy to support the development of secure products with digital elements and manage vulnerabilities?
area-1.OSO1.questions.Q2.text: Does the cybersecurity policy include procedures for documenting, resolving, and eliminating vulnerabilities?
area-1.OSO1.questions.Q3.text: Does this policy include voluntary vulnerability reporting in accordance with Article 15?
area-1.OSO2.hint:
Be prepared to cooperate with market surveillance authorities when requested, in order to help mitigate cybersecurity risks related to open-source products with digital elements.

You must also be able to provide documentation of your cybersecurity policy—as required under your internal procedures—in a clear and understandable language for the authority, and in paper or electronic form upon a reasoned request.
area-1.OSO2.questions.Q1.text: Does the organization have procedures or established arrangements for cooperating with market surveillance authorities, upon request, to mitigate cybersecurity risks related to products with digital elements?
area-1.OSO2.questions.Q2.text: Upon a reasoned request from the market surveillance authority, are the open-source stewards able to provide the relevant documentation on their cybersecurity policy, in a language easily understood, in paper or electronic form?
area-1.OSO3.hint:
If you are involved in the development of open-source products with digital elements, you must implement procedures that meet the following obligations:

Notify any actively exploited vulnerabilities you become aware of, simultaneously to the designated CSIRT coordinator and to ENISA, using the single reporting platform defined under Article 16.

Notify any severe security incidents affecting the product’s security, also simultaneously to the CSIRT coordinator and ENISA via the same reporting platform.

Inform affected users promptly about actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. This communication should include, where appropriate, detailed information on risks and available mitigation or corrective measures. Information should be provided in a clear and, if possible, machine-readable format to allow automatic processing.

In cases where timely user notification is not possible, CSIRTs may intervene to provide necessary information to users to prevent or mitigate harm.

Additionally, ensure you have processes in place to share information about vulnerabilities with the open-source community and to keep users informed transparently about security issues.
area-1.OSO3.questions.Q1.text: Have appropriate procedures been implemented for reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities and serious security incidents of the product to CSIRT/ENISA?
area-1.OSO3.questions.Q2.text: Does the organization have a procedure or established practice for sharing information about detected vulnerabilities with the open-source community?
area-1.OSO3.questions.Q3.text: Does the organization have a procedure for informing users about actively exploited vulnerabilities, including, when necessary, additional details and information on available mitigating or corrective measures?
area-1.OSO3.questions.Q4.text: Does the organization have a procedure for informing users about serious security incidents, including, when necessary, additional details about the incident, its severity, and any available corrective or mitigating measures?
